policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 2 Jan close (1x4 3.79, 3x6 3.56, 6x9 3.36, 9x12 3.33 vs WIBOR 3M 3.97) price roughly 60bp of NBP cuts within 12 months. The NBP survey of professional forecasters (published 2 Jan) sees an average reference rate of 3.69% in 2026; December economist calls cluster at 3.50% by mid-2026 and 3.25% by end-2026 (ING). Governor Glapiński (4 Dec): 4% is 'excellent' for now; the MPC is in wait-and-see.
policy.risk_text: MPC members ruled out a January cut (Kotecki 10 Dec; Wnorowski and Kotecki 16 Dec: no change at the next two meetings). If cuts are pushed out, front-end roll-down does not materialise; Santander (9 Dec) expected higher short-end yields in Q1 as cut expectations are repriced.

macro.projection_text: NBP November 2025 projection: CPI 3.7% (2025), 2.9% (2026), 2.5% (2027); December 2025 flash CPI 2.4% y/y.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit ~6.9% of GDP (MoF plan); 2026 budget deficit cap PLN 271.7bn, gross borrowing needs ~PLN 690bn; Santander (19 Dec) noted the 10Y ASW back near 100bp on global fiscal worries.
macro.fiscal_risk_text: Q1 2026 supply of PLN 75-100bn over 8 auctions; Fitch (27 Feb) and Moody's (20 Mar) reviews with negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP cut six times in 2025 to 4.00% (last on 3 Dec) and signalled a pause; CPI fell to 2.4% in December (flash, 31 Dec), and the NBP projects 2.9% for 2026 (professional forecasters, 2 Jan: 2.6%). Manufacturing PMI fell to 48.5 in December (2 Jan; consensus ~49.3), the eighth month below 50. GDP grew 3.8% y/y in Q3. MoF had pre-financed ~23% of 2026 gross needs by 31 Dec with ~PLN 143bn of budget cash. Ratings: Fitch A- negative (5 Sep), Moody's A2 negative (19 Sep), S&P A- stable (7 Nov). Street views (December): PKO 1Q26 forecast 2Y 3.75 / 5Y 4.50 / 10Y 5.10; Pekao expects yields to drift lower as cuts are priced; Santander expects higher yields in Q1 on supply and cut repricing; ING says early-2026 trading will follow MoF's Q1 issuance. Weekend news before Monday's open (3-4 Jan): a US strike on Venezuela (3 Jan) and Ukraine peace meetings scheduled for 3, 6 and 7 Jan - global risk/oil headlines to watch at the open.

calendar.plan_text: MoF Q1 2026 financing plan (31 Dec 2025): 8 sale auctions for PLN 75-100bn, one switch auction, possible foreign issuance. January: sale auctions on 9 Jan (PLN 7-12bn), 22 Jan (8-13bn) and 28 Jan (7-12bn). 2026 gross borrowing needs ~PLN 690bn, ~23% pre-financed at year-end; budget cash ~PLN 143bn. BGK: FPC to issue domestically in 2026 (up to PLN 18.5bn); the defence fund (FWSZ) to rely mainly on EU SAFE and export-credit loans (BGK, 29 Dec). Series for the 9 Jan auction had not been announced by 4 Jan.
calendar.timing_text: Within each auction week of the Aug-Dec 2025 sample, yields drifted lower into the auction (rally regime) and the auction-day close was the cheapest point relative to the preceding session, so new buying is best executed at the auction-day close (9, 22, 28 Jan) rather than the day before. January supply is front-loaded (PLN 22-37bn across three auctions) after only ~23% pre-financing. For the front end the 13-14 Jan MPC is the event: members pre-announced no January cut, so a hold is the base case; the December final CPI (mid-January) and the February/March meetings drive the cut timing.
